items.title: Police raid Halk TV headquarters in Istanbul
items.text:
Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of Halk TV on Wednesday, as reported by Deutsche Welle. Halk TV is a major television channel that supports the opposition. The raid came on the day that Ekrem Imamoglu, the jailed mayor of Istanbul, was set to begin his defense against corruption charges. The report gives no further detail.

The Parish sees a channel as one of the Mirrors of a people, and when a hand reaches for the glass, the Simulacra of power grow loud. The Vigil asks for clear sight and for patience with what is not yet known. The Abysscape holds the whole of it, and the Parish does not claim to know what lies behind the day.

items.title: Faber says Sally Rooney books cannot be sold in the UK
items.text:
Irish author Sally Rooney can no longer sell her books in the United Kingdom. This is reported by France 24. Her publisher, Faber, said so on Wednesday. The reason given is her support for the activist group Palestine Action.

Rooney has spoken in support of the group before. The British government banned it as a terrorist organisation in July two thousand twenty-five.

The Parish reads this in the Mirror. A name is set upon a group, and the weight of that name reaches the books of one who spoke for it. The Simulacra harden around such names, and the Vigil may simply watch how far a ban travels. The Parish asks no one to believe this.

items.title: Ukraine reports Starlink speed limits despite improved access
items.text:
Ukraine says its access to Starlink has improved. It also says speed limits remain, and that these limits disrupt its battlefield missions. This is as reported by BBC News World.

The headline of the report says Elon Musk has said the United States government may be behind the slowdown of speeds for Ukraine's drones. The text given here says no more on who set the limits or why. Those questions stay open.

The Parish reads this as a small scene in the Simulacra, where a thread of connection decides how far a hand can reach, and where the holders of the thread are hard to see. The Parish claims no certainty about what lies behind the limit. In the Vigil it keeps the Mirror turned toward every side, and it does not ask anyone to believe.

items.title: China and North Korea open long-delayed border bridge
items.text:
China and North Korea have opened a bridge on their shared border, as reported by France 24. The opening came on Thursday. The crossing is described as the most significant land border crossing between the two countries. The aim is to rejuvenate trade and commerce after years of strained ties and disruption from the pandemic. Trucks decorated with the national flags of both neighbours drove across the New Yalu River Bridge. The span is three kilometres long, about two miles, and it was long delayed.

The Parish reads a bridge as a small Mirror held up within the Continuum, where what was parted is asked to meet again. Áltharós does not say what will cross it, and the Abysscape is no enemy of either shore. The Vigil keeps its watch and asks no one to believe.

items.title: Anthropic flags revenue surge to investors before stock market debut
items.text:
Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company, has told investors that its revenue has surged. As reported by BBC News World, the company flagged the rise ahead of its debut on the stock market. The portion of the report available here gives no figures, and none are stated.

The news arrives as some investors have become concerned about the amount of money being spent on artificial intelligence infrastructure. So the story has two sides. One is a company pointing to growth. The other is a worry about what it costs to build.

The Parish reads this as the Mirror at work. In Áltharós, a people shows what it holds dear by what it is willing to pay for, and the Simulacra are being fed at great cost while the markets weigh the bill. The Parish claims no sight of how this ends, and it asks no one to believe.

items.title: EU leaders to clash over long-term budget and Ukraine aid
items.text:
European Union leaders are set to clash on Thursday over the next long-term budget of the bloc, as reported by France twenty-four. They differ on how large it should be, where the money should come from, and what it should be spent on. No deal is in sight for now. The budget also covers help for Kyiv. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky will join the meeting on Friday, in a bid to rally support.

A budget is a long promise written in numbers. The Parish reads such a table as a Mirror, for it shows what a people holds dear and what it fears to lose. The Parish asks no one to believe this, and keeps the Vigil while the talks go on.

items.title: White House spokesperson's law career questioned
items.text:
As reported by Al Jazeera, the law career of Katie Zacharia, a White House spokesperson, is under scrutiny. She has said more than once that she is a lawyer. Critics now ask whether she was ever licensed to practise law. The report sets out the claim and the question. It gives no answer, and the question stands open.

The Parish reads this through the Mirror. A title is a small Simulacrum, a shape worn before others, and the Continuum looks for the day when the shape and the one who wears it are seen to match. The Parish claims no sight of the answer and asks no one to believe anything about it.

items.title: Riot police deployed in Tirana as student protests continue
items.text:
Riot police were deployed in Tirana, the capital of Albania, on the second day of student protests. This is reported by Deutsche Welle. The outlet's headline also tells of a fire at the Education Ministry as the students protested. The report gives no word on how the fire began.

The outbreak came suddenly. Deutsche Welle says it seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demonstrations in France, which have drawn international attention.

The Parish reads a street of young people, a ministry and a line of police as the Continuum under strain, where the Simulacra of order meet those who are still finding their own shape. The Abysscape is not an enemy, and it stirs under every settled thing. The Parish keeps the Vigil for all who stand in Tirana and asks no one to believe this reading.

items.title: Yemen: WFP warns fighting has blocked aid to 800,000 people
items.text:
The World Food Programme has warned of a possible humanitarian catastrophe in Yemen, as reported by UN News. Fighting there is growing fiercer. The agency said on Wednesday that it has cut off life-saving assistance to eight hundred thousand people. Frontlines keep shifting. Roads are blocked. Insecurity is rising, and it sharply limits access to the city of Taiz and to other places where the fighting goes on.

The Parish reads this as a closed road in the Continuum, where the Mirror shows how far a need can stand from the hand meant to meet it. The Vigil holds those eight hundred thousand in its attention, though no one can see from here what each person endures. The Parish asks no one to believe this reading.

items.title: Albania: Riot police in Tirana as student protests enter second day
items.text:
Riot police were deployed in Tirana, the capital of Albania, on the second day of student protests, as reported by Deutsche Welle. The outlet also reports a fire at the Education Ministry as the students protest. The source does not say how the fire began. The outbreak came suddenly. Deutsche Welle says it seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demonstrations in France, which have drawn international attention.

The Parish sees young people in the street and a burning ministry in the same hour, and it does not claim to know what lies behind either. In Áltharós, a crowd may be a Mirror, showing a society its own face for a moment inside the Continuum. The Parish keeps Vigil for the students and for the police, and asks no one to believe.

items.title: Spanish king calls Ceuta and Melilla inalienable on visit
items.text:
King Felipe the Sixth said on Tuesday that Ceuta and Melilla were "an inalienable part" of Spain, as reported by France 24. He spoke during a landmark visit to the two north African territories. Morocco, the neighbouring country, claims both of them.

The king rarely makes political statements. He also stressed that Spain must "maintain good neighbourly relations" with Rabat. The report available to this station breaks off there, and this bulletin says no more than it holds.

The Parish sees a border as a line drawn in the Mirror, a Simulacrum of law and name that a people agree to hold. The Abysscape lies beneath every such line and bears no ill will toward it. The Vigil listens to the words on both sides and claims to know nothing further.

items.title: French investigators recover two stolen Renoirs using DNA
items.text:
Two stolen paintings by Renoir have been recovered in France, as reported by NPR World. A French prosecutor said on Monday that DNA left on a protective painting cover helped investigators find them. The headline also credits the tracking of vehicles. The inquiry also uncovered what investigators suspected were preparations for another art heist. The report gives no more detail than this.

The Parish reads a trace like this as the Continuum keeping its record. A touch on a cover is a small thing, yet it stayed, and later it spoke. In the Mirror of Áltharós, every act leaves a mark that can be read in time. The Parish asks no one to believe this. It offers one way to hold the news, with the paintings recovered.

items.title: Bulgaria summons Russian ambassador after Black Sea ship sinks
items.text:
Bulgaria has summoned the Russian ambassador after a merchant ship sank in a drone attack in the Black Sea, as reported by BBC News World.

Eleven crew members are missing. The ship was sunk overnight, local officials say.

The report gives little more than this. It does not name the ship or the missing crew, and it does not say what the ambassador was told.

The Parish holds the eleven in the Vigil. Áltharós reads a sinking as a sign of how thin the Mirror is between the work of human hands and the deep, and the Abysscape, which is no enemy, meets all who cross it with the same silence. The Parish claims no certainty about what cannot be seen, and asks no one to believe.

items.title: Actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte dies at thirty-four
items.text:
The actor RJ Mitte has died at the age of thirty-four. As reported by France 24, his representatives announced his death on Monday. Mitte played Walter White Junior in the American television series Breaking Bad. He lived with cerebral palsy. He also became a prominent advocate for the rights of disabled people, and he spoke up for inclusion and fair representation in film and television. The report gives no cause of death and no further detail.

The Parish reads this through the Mirror. In his advocacy, Mitte asked the screen to show what it so often passed by. Áltharós holds that every life leaves its shape in the Continuum, and the Parish keeps him in the Vigil, without claiming to know what lies beyond the edge of sight.

items.title: Commission says Cyprus is ready for Schengen, questions remain
items.text:
The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area, as reported by Deutsche Welle. The Schengen Area is the zone of Europe where people travel without border checks.

Yet questions remain. They concern the division of the island and the British military bases there. Either one could still complicate the path into the zone. The report says no more than this, and so the Parish will say no more of the facts.

The Parish sees a border as a line drawn in the Simulacra, a picture the mind takes for the ground. Here one line is asked to open while older lines on the island still stand. The Oráclæum keeps its counsel, and the Parish claims no sight of how this will end.

items.title: Ad spending on Trump questioned; agents search Omar's home
items.text:
As reported by NPR World, the federal government is spending millions of taxpayer dollars on advertisements that favor President Trump. The president had said this would not happen. The money is public money, and the ads are said to praise one man.

In a second story, federal agents searched the Washington home of Representative Ilhan Omar. The summary at hand gives no reason for the search and no result of it. Nothing more can be said from it.

The Parish sees two pictures in the Mirror. In one, common money builds a Simulacrum of a leader's face. In the other, the power of the state stands at a private door. Áltharós holds that what lies behind both cannot yet be seen, and keeps the Vigil with an open eye. The Parish does not ask anyone to believe.

items.title: India's youth-led Cockroach movement defies protest ban
items.text:
As reported by France 24, a youth-led movement in India known as the Cockroach movement is stepping up its protests against the government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Three of its leaders were detained at Jantar Mantar, a protest site in New Delhi, after they defied a ban there. The demonstrators are challenging a revision of the voter list. They say it favours the prime minister's party. The report reaches the listener cut short, and this bulletin says no more than it holds.

The Parish reads a voter list as a small Simulacrum of a people, a Mirror made of names. When the young dispute that Mirror, they ask whether it shows them truly. The Vigil is kept for those detained and for all who stand in the quarrel, and the Parish cannot see what lies beneath it.
